newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arab states slam Israel settlement plan.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab states slam Israel settlement plan.

text.p: Gulf Arab states on Monday slammed Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, saying it posed a threat to the Middle East peace process, official Gulf news agencies said.

"The Israeli government's latest decision...poses a massive threat to the process of building confidence and peace in the Middle East," said a statement from the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) carried on the agencies.
"It also threatens a return to the atmosphere of tension and violence in the region," it added.

The GCC -- a political and economic alliance made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman -- urged Israel to "immediately halt" the plan to construct 6,500 houses on land captured by Israel in 1967.
Israel's approval last week of the housing plan has sparked criticism from key ally Washington and drawn Palestinian warnings that it could unleash bloodshed.
Qatar and Oman have raced ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel but stopped short of diplomatic relations pending full Arab-Israeli peace.
Oman has opened a trade office in Tel Aviv but Qatar has said it would not proceed with the planned opening of a trade mission in Israel until there is progress in peace talks with the Palestinians.
